📚 The Heidegger Controversy (Philosophy, Politics, and the Question of National Socialism) | Author: Jürg Altwegg | Translator: Seyyed Amin al-Din Abtahi | First Edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publications | 2026 | The Heidegger Controversy is a vivid account of one of the greatest philosophical crises of the twentieth century: the confrontation of Europe's intellectual world with Martin Heidegger's National Socialist past. This book is a collection of articles, documents, letters, and dialogues that record the reaction of German-speaking intellectuals, especially the French, to Victor Farias's revelations about Heidegger's role in the Nazi regime; revelations that showed that the philosopher who, for post-war generations in France, was a theoretical authority and an intellectual pillar for existentialism and resistance against totalitarianism, had himself once been at the heart of the Nazi machine. The Heidegger Controversy places the reader at the center of a fundamental debate: Can a clear line be drawn between philosophy and politics? entry.title: 📚 Journalism of War and Peace | Author: Abdolreza Aalami | First Edition |…
entry.summary:
Source: @bijanabdolkarimi

📚 Journalism of War and Peace | Author: Abdolreza Aalami | First Edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publications | 2026 | In a world where every armed conflict is narrated on news pages and in cyberspace before it is decided on the battlefield, this is the fundamental question: What responsibility does a journalist have? This book examines two distinct approaches to media coverage of conflicts: war journalism, which focuses on violence, dramatization, and winner-loser narratives, and peace journalism, which places the roots of conflict, hidden voices, and ways out at the center of attention. These two approaches not only define the method of reporting but also influence public opinion, political decisions, and even the course of conflicts. Drawing on the theories of Johan Galtung, the founder of the concept of peace journalism, and the views of Jake Lynch and Annabel McGoldrick, this book blends theory with field experience. Case studies from Gaza, Ukraine, Syria, and Sudan show how editorial choices, from camera angle to source selection, can make war seem natural or peace possible. The book also addresses the new challenges of journalism in the digital age: cyber warfare, misinformation, and cyberspace as a parallel battlefield whose rules are still being formed. This book is written for journalism and communications students, field journalists, and any curious reader who wants to understand how the media narrate war—and what that narration costs. The media is not a mirror of reality, but its constructor. 🛒Click on this link to buy the book🛒🟠Join Naqd-e Farhang on Instagram🟠@naqdefarhangpub.

entry.summary:
Source: @bijanabdolkarimi

📚 Being and Language (An Exploration of Linguistic and Meaning Foundations) | Author: Seyyed Javad Miri | First Edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publications | 2026 | Is language merely a tool for communication and a field for political struggles, or is it the fundamental horizon of our being? In this book, the author, moving beyond the teachings of classical and contemporary philosophers, examines the inseparable bond between 'Being' and 'language.' While in common discourses language is often reduced to a political tool or a social construct, this book invites the reader to recognize the ontological essence of language. Drawing on the great philosophical traditions, this work argues that language is the open domain in which reality is revealed to us. Speaking is not merely an act, but our way of dwelling in the world. By going beyond instrumental approaches, this book re-presents language as the primary locus of the connection between being and human understanding; that is, the silent architecture of the world in which we live. 🛒Click on this link to buy the book🛒🟠Join Naqd-e Farhang on Instagram🟠@naqdefarhangpub.
